headline: Learned cancer models reused across cohorts and layers, judged on generalisation
label: Transfer Learning In Cancer Omics
summary: Models trained on one cohort, cancer type or omics layer are now tested for reuse and generalisation in new patient populations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of learned structure across cohorts, cancer types, or data layers. A layer-specific transfer elastic net borrows from older breast cancer cohorts to predict survival in patients under 50, and a cross-cancer study assesses the applicability of an axillary lymph node deep-learning model to metastasis prediction. Other items test whether models generalise rather than whether they transfer: a multimodal deep model for ER, PR and HER2 status reports strong cross-cohort AUCs alongside poor calibration and no gain over a 3-gene baseline. CAISL anchors lung adenocarcinoma survival learning to clinical variables with sparse molecular risk correction, evaluated on TCGA. A TCGA classification study finds logistic regression strongest among five learners and three ensembles. Across the set, evaluation, particularly calibration and comparison against simple baselines, is the sharper point.
